title: Critical Thinking
overview: Critical thinking is the disciplined process of examining information, assumptions, arguments, and evidence before reaching conclusions or making decisions. In modern workplaces, professionals are continuously exposed to large volumes of information, competing viewpoints, incomplete data, persuasive messages, and time-sensitive problems. The ability to think critically helps individuals move beyond first impressions and habitual responses toward more reasoned, evidence-based judgments.

The Critical Thinking course is designed to strengthen participants’ ability to analyze situations objectively, ask purposeful questions, distinguish facts from assumptions and opinions, evaluate the quality and relevance of evidence, identify weaknesses in reasoning, and construct sound conclusions. Participants will explore practical frameworks that can be applied to everyday workplace problems, discussions, proposals, reports, meetings, and decisions.

The program also develops awareness of cognitive biases and thinking traps that can distort judgment. Participants will practice recognizing assumptions, considering alternative explanations, testing claims, comparing options, and communicating reasoning clearly and constructively.

Through case studies, structured questioning, problem-solving exercises, argument analysis, decision scenarios, and reflective activities, participants will develop a practical critical-thinking approach that supports better judgment, stronger problem solving, more effective decision-making, and greater confidence when dealing with complex or ambiguous situations.
audience: This course is suitable for managers, supervisors, team leaders, professionals, analysts, administrators, project team members, customer-facing employees, and other individuals whose roles require problem solving, evaluation of information, decision-making, or the communication of recommendations. It is particularly beneficial for professionals who need to assess competing viewpoints, work with incomplete or complex information, challenge assumptions constructively, and make well-reasoned decisions in the workplace.
methodology: The course uses an interactive and application-focused methodology combining short instructor-led presentations with individual thinking exercises, case studies, workplace scenarios, structured questioning, argument analysis, group discussions, problem-solving activities, decision simulations, and reflective assessments. Participants will examine realistic claims and situations, identify assumptions and biases, evaluate evidence, compare alternative interpretations, and practice explaining the reasoning behind their conclusions. The methodology emphasizes practical transfer to workplace decisions and encourages participants to develop a repeatable critical-thinking process that can be used after the course.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the principles and workplace value of critical thinking.
Distinguish facts, opinions, assumptions, interpretations, and inferences when evaluating information.
Apply structured questioning techniques to clarify issues and uncover missing information.
Identify assumptions and test whether they are reasonable and adequately supported.
Evaluate the credibility, relevance, sufficiency, and consistency of evidence.
Analyze arguments by identifying claims, reasons, evidence, and conclusions.
Recognize common logical fallacies, cognitive biases, and thinking traps that can weaken judgment.
Consider alternative explanations and perspectives before reaching conclusions.
Apply systematic approaches to define and analyze workplace problems.
Compare options using explicit criteria and make more defensible decisions.
Communicate conclusions and recommendations using clear, evidence-based reasoning.
Develop an individual action plan for applying critical thinking in daily professional situations.
